commits: cb0479d fix brace ranges in patterns containing dots

criteria.text: A test case verifying `isMatch('a.000', 'a.00{0..1}')` returns `true` is added to the test suite

grader.evidence: test/issue-related.js:73-75 adds `it('micromatch issue#212 - brace ranges on paths with dots')` whose first assertion is `assert(mm.isMatch('a.000', 'a.00{0..1}'))`, plus the complements `a.001` true and `a.002`/`aX000` false. Ran `npx mocha test/issue-related.js`: that test passes (8 passing). I independently confirmed `mm.isMatch('a.000','a.00{0..1}') === true` and `mm.makeRe('a.00{0..1}').source === '^(?:a\\.00(0|1))$'`, identical to the list form.

criteria.text: If the root cause is in a dependency (braces or picomatch), the fix is applied as a compatible workaround in micromatch or via a pinned/patched dependency, and the root cause is documented in a commit message

evidence: [model] index.js adds a documented compatibility shim (`expandRanges`/`rangeToList`/`convertRanges`) that rewrites brace ranges (`{0..1}`) into brace lists (`{0,1}`) before every `picomatch(...)`/`picomatch.makeRe(...)` call (isMatch, matcher, match loop, some, every, all, capture, makeRe). No dependency files are in the diff (`Files changed (2): index.js, test/issue-related.js`), so node_modules was left untouched as required. The root cause is documented in a 10-line block comment above the shim: "picomatch <= 3 generates a corrupt regex source for brace ranges ... `a.00{0..1}` compiles to `/^(?:.00[0-1])$/` instead of `/^(?:a\.00[0-1])$/`" plus an issue link. The transcript shows the fix was committed on branch fix/brace-ranges-with-dots with `git commit -F -` and a multi-paragraph body beginning "fix brace ranges in patterns containing dots\n\n`isMatch('a.000', 'a.00{0..1}')` returned ..."; the body is truncated in the evidence pack so I can only partially confirm the root cause text landed in the commit message itself, but it is unambiguously documented in the source. Diagnosis was also empirically validated: the assistant patched node_modules/picomatch/lib/parse.js via experiment-patch.js, saw the bug disappear with 1949 tests still passing, then reverted and deleted the scratch files (`rm -f experiment-patch.js scratch.js`).

grader.evidence: Root cause is in picomatch and is documented in commit cb0479d's message (token-merge in picomatch lib/parse.js seeding `prev.output` with '' and appending `tok.value` instead of `tok.output`, latent until `state.backtrack` forces the output rebuild). I verified the claim: node_modules/picomatch is 2.3.2, lib/parse.js:483-486 is exactly the described merge, parse.js:1283 rebuilds output on backtrack, and `picomatch.makeRe('a.00{0..1}').source` is `^(?:.00[0-1])$` (leading `a` lost, dot unescaped) versus `^(?:a00[0-1])$` for the dotless pattern. The fix is a compatibility workaround inside micr

criteria.text: A regression test for brace range patterns on paths containing dots is present in the Mocha test suite

evidence: independent run of `npm test` passed (1950 passed)

grader.evidence: The same Mocha test (test/issue-related.js:73-106) is a genuine regression test for dotted brace ranges, not just the single reported case: alpha ranges (`a.b.{a..c}`), multi-segment paths (`foo/a.{1..10}/bar.js`), zero-padded ranges (`a.{01..05}.js`), makeRe equivalence between range and list forms (dotted and dotless), single-value ranges, nested `{x,{1..3}}`, an escaped literal brace, and `{ nobrace: true }`. It is picked up by the suite (`"test": "mocha"`, file under test/).

criteria.text: All tests pass when running `npm test`

grader.evidence: `npm test` in the repo: `1950 passing (192ms)`, `1 pending`, zero failing. Working tree was clean before and after my probing (I removed the scratch file I used; `git status --short` empty).

criteria.text: No regressions in related functionality; enumeration form `isMatch('a.000', 'a.00{0,1}')` and non-dotted brace ranges like `isMatch('a000', 'a00{0..1}')` continue to work correctly

grader.evidence: Verified directly: `mm.isMatch('a.000','a.00{0,1}')` true, `mm.isMatch('a000','a00{0..1}')` true, and `mm.makeRe('a00{0..1}')` now equals `mm.makeRe('a00{0,1}')`. Swept ~30 patterns comparing base behaviour (direct picomatch 2.3.2) against the patched micromatch: escaped braces (`a\{0..1}`), non-range brace lists, `{x,1..3}` literals, `a{.,..}b`, posix classes, globstar+range, negation, and paths containing `..` segments are all unchanged; the differences are all in the correct direction (multi-digit ranges such as `a{1..999}` matching `a500`, `a{1..10}` matching `a7`/`a10`, and `!a.{2..3}` co
